what_its_for: Clotrimazole is an antifungal medicine used to treat fungal infections of the skin, mouth, and vagina. It helps get rid of infections like athlete's foot, jock itch, ringworm, yeast infections (vaginal thrush), and oral thrush (fungal infection in the mouth). It works by killing the fungus that is causing your infection.
how_to_take: How you use clotrimazole depends on what form you have been given: CREAM or LOTION (for skin): Wash and dry the affected area of skin first. Apply a thin layer of cream to the infected area and a little bit of the skin around it. Gently rub it in. Wash your hands before and after applying, unless you are treating your hands. VAGINAL CREAM or PESSARY (for vaginal infections): Use the applicator provided to insert the cream or tablet deep into your vagina at bedtime. Lie down afterward to help the medicine stay in place. LOZENGE or TROCHE (for mouth infections): Let the lozenge dissolve slowly in your mouth. Do NOT chew or swallow it whole. Do not eat or drink for 30 minutes after using it.
dosing: Always follow your doctor or pharmacist's instructions. Typical dosing is: SKIN infections: Apply 2 times a day (morning and night) for 2 to 4 weeks. VAGINAL infections: Use once a day at bedtime for 3 to 7 days depending on the product. MOUTH infections (lozenge): Dissolve one lozenge in your mouth 5 times a day for 14 days. Do not use more than directed or for longer than recommended.
missed_dose: If you forget a dose, use or apply it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do NOT use a double dose to make up for a missed one. Try to use your medicine at the same time each day to help you remember.
storage: Store clotrimazole at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, direct sunlight, and moisture. Do NOT freeze the cream or vaginal products. Keep the cap tightly closed when not in use. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not flush unused medicine down the toilet. Ask your pharmacist about the best way to dispose of medicine you no longer need.
what_to_avoid: Avoid getting clotrimazole cream or lotion in your eyes, nose, or mouth. If contact occurs, rinse thoroughly with water. Do not cover treated skin with airtight bandages or wrappings unless your doctor tells you to. Avoid wearing tight-fitting or synthetic (non-breathable) clothing over infected skin areas, as this can make the infection worse. For vaginal products, avoid sexual intercourse during treatment. Note that vaginal clotrimazole can weaken condoms and diaphragms, so use another form of birth control during treatment and for a few days after. Do not use tampons, douches, or other vaginal products while using vaginal clotrimazole unless your doctor says it is okay.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor or get medical help if: Your symptoms do not improve after 1 to 2 weeks of treatment, or get worse at any time. You develop a rash, hives, blistering, or severe irritation in the treated area. You have unusual swelling, redness, or pain that is getting worse. You experience difficulty breathing or swallowing, which could be a sign of a serious allergic reaction — call 911 or go to the emergency room immediately. For vaginal infections: you have fever, chills, or abdominal pain along with your symptoms. You are not sure if your symptoms are from a fungal infection. This is your first vaginal infection — see a doctor to confirm the diagnosis before using this medicine.
when_it_works: You may start to feel better within a few days of starting clotrimazole. However, it is very important to continue using the medicine for the full length of time prescribed or recommended, even if your symptoms go away. Stopping too early can allow the infection to come back. Skin infections like athlete's foot may take 2 to 4 weeks to fully clear up. Vaginal infections often improve within 3 to 7 days. Mouth infections usually improve within a few days but may need 14 days of treatment.
special_populations: PREGNANCY: If you are pregnant, speak with your doctor before using clotrimazole, especially vaginal products. The vaginal applicator should be used with extra care during pregnancy. Skin creams are generally considered safer. BREASTFEEDING: Talk to your doctor before using clotrimazole if you are breastfeeding. Do not apply it to the nipple or breast area if you are nursing. CHILDREN: Clotrimazole skin creams may be used in children under doctor supervision. Vaginal products are not recommended for girls under 12 years of age without a doctor's advice. Oral lozenges are generally used in adults and children over 3 years of age. ELDERLY: No special dose changes are usually needed for older adults, but speak with your doctor or pharmacist if you have any concerns. LIVER PROBLEMS: If you have liver disease, let your doctor know, especially when using the oral lozenge form, as it may need to be monitored more closely.
